strings.name: Marco Rubio
strings.role: Politician · US secretary of state and national security adviser
strings.summary: From a Cuban immigrant family in Miami, Rubio trained in law and moved from local politics to Florida’s legislature, becoming House speaker. A US senator from 2011 to 2025, he worked on foreign affairs, intelligence and national security and sought the 2016 presidential nomination. He became secretary of state in 2025, additionally acting as national security adviser; that role became permanent in 2026, placing him at the center of Trump’s foreign policy.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Through long involvement in US Senate foreign affairs and national security, his foreign-policy positions affect relations across the Americas and globally.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Bachelor’s degree from the University of Florida and law degree from the University of Miami; later worked in law and local public affairs.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Senate foreign and security work
strings.highlights.h1.text: Served on foreign-relations and intelligence committees and advanced legislation concerning China, Cuba and the Americas.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Dual foreign-policy and security roles
strings.highlights.h2.text: Became secretary of state in 2025 and, after acting service, permanent national security adviser in 2026.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Became permanent national security adviser
strings.timeline.t1.text: The White House made permanent the acting role he held from May 2025, alongside the State Department.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Became secretary of state
strings.timeline.t2.text: After Senate confirmation, was sworn in as the 72nd secretary and left the Senate.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Advanced forced-labor legislation
strings.timeline.t3.text: Helped advance the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act, affecting trade and human-rights policy.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Ended presidential primary campaign
strings.timeline.t4.text: Suspended his bid after losing Florida’s Republican primary, then sought Senate reelection.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Entered US Senate
strings.timeline.t5.text: Began representing Florida, serving until moving to the executive branch in 2025.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Became Florida House speaker
strings.timeline.t6.text: Led the state House of Representatives until 2008.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Entered state legislature
strings.timeline.t7.text: Won a special election to the Florida House after local service in West Miami.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed law degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Earned his law degree at Miami before beginning legal and political work.
